sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Precision Steel Injection Molding of Color Snap-Fit Plastic Kits

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate tax or registry distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (civil-law foundation with strong Anglo-American corporate and commercial law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012; investment chapter governs U.S.–Panama investment protection)
Panama–Singapore Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force 2018)
Panama–Netherlands Convention on the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force 2005)
Panama–Spain Convention on the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force 2014)
Panama–Mexico Convention on the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force 2017)
Panama–United Arab Emirates Convention on the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT due-diligence regime), as amended, with Executive Decree No. 201 of 2 November 2016; Decree-Law No. 2 of 2011 establishing the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); Law No. 129 of 18 March 2020 and DGI Resolution No. 201-1698 of 30 April 2021 (Mandatory Beneficial Owner Registry); Law No. 32 of 1927 on Sociedades Anónimas, as amended; Public Registry electronic-filing regulations (Acuerdo No. 79 of 2022). FATF grey-list removal (October 2023) obliges continued compliance with enhanced BO reporting and risk-based supervision.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner's valid international passport (biographical page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 HCCH Convention, in force for Panama since 1991) OR Consular Legalization via a Panamanian consulate for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the UBO or corporate shareholder (issued within the preceding three months) and/or proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank or utility provider in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate shareholder (where the S.A. is formed within a corporate chain)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the Panamanian incorporating attorney and resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of execution (executed by the UBO or authorized director)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; a certified original must accompany the notarized copy for protocol

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Directors/Officers of the shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the shareholder entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional/AML reference letter from the introducing foreign counsel or escrow bank (executed under penalty of perjury)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualifying foreign counsel or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; alternatively delivered direct to counsel subject to Law 23 of 2015 risk-based outsourcing rules

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 de la República de Panamá (Ley General de Sociedades), as amended by Ley 5 de 2018 (private-instrument incorporation and governance modernization) and Ley 70 de 2018 (beneficial ownership declaration regime), together with the resident-agent requirements of Ley 52 de 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil (Corporate Registry Section), Panamá City headquarters and provincial windows; filings may be presented through the Registro Público online services portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública No. ___ de Constitución executed before a Notary Public of Panama, or a Pacto Social y Estatutos constituted as a private instrument under Ley 5 de 2018, presented for inscription in the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Authorized capital of no less than USD 10,000 must be declared in the articles of incorporation (Ley 32 de 1927, Art. 1). No statutory escrow deposit or mandatory lump-sum payment is required at formation; the subscriber may execute a qualified declaration that the subscribed capital is fully paid, and the Registry does not verify actual bank deposit. Foreign shareholders may hold 100% of the issued shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscription of one hundred (100) ordinary shares subscribed by the founding shareholder, and that such subscription is declared fully paid. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be maintained at the offices of [Resident Agent Name], who is appointed resident agent for service of process in Panama. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that [President Name], [Secretary Name], and [Treasurer Name] are appointed President, Secretary, and Treasurer, respectively, to serve one-year terms. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the President and Treasurer, acting jointly, are authorized to open bank accounts, execute manufacturing, supply, and licensing contracts, and affix the corporate seal to instruments in the ordinary course of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — corporate name reservation desk / online 'Servicios en Línea del Registro Público' portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability application for the proposed corporate name (e.g., '[Target Name], S.A.') through the Registro Público online portal or the Mercantil window. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain the Certificado de Registro de Nombre, which reserves the name for a statutory validity period (60 days) pending inscription of the incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee (approx. USD 50)
Copy of the applicant's passport or Panamanian cédula
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for identity or deceptive similarity to an existing registered company, file a written reconsideration with the Registro Público within the curing period or reserve an alternative distinguishable name; names creating likelihood of confusion cannot be registered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the articles of incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (notarial deed route) or executing attorneys under Ley 5 de 2018 (private instrument route)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the incorporation instrument in Spanish, containing the corporate name, registered office, resident agent appointment, authorized capital of at least USD 10,000, share classes, board of directors, and the broad corporate purpose covering manufacture, import, distribution, and sale of toys, games, and plastic injection-molded articles. Execute before a Panama Notary with all incorporators, or execute as a private document signed by all incorporators and ratified before a notary as required by Ley 5 de 2018.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos or Escritura Pública)
Passport copies of all incorporators and directors
Proof of residential address of each director (utility bill or bank reference)
Resident agent acceptance letter from a licensed Panamanian law firm or agent
KYC / due diligence forms and beneficial ownership statement
Declaration of qualified payment of subscribed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If drafting defects, missing notarial legalizations, or incomplete shareholder signatures are detected, execute a corrective addendum (adenda) before the same notary and re-file the instrument with the Registro Público.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Registro Público (acquisition of legal personality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil (corporate inscription window or online e-filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated copy of the incorporation instrument, the name reservation certificate, the resident agent consent, and proof of payment of the registry fees to the Sección Mercantil. The Registry legally examines the instrument for conformity with Ley 32 de 1927; upon approval it grants the inscription (inscripción), which confers juridical personality, and issues a stamped certified copy of the inscribed articles.
required_dossiers: Authenticated copy of the Escritura Pública or Pacto Social
Corporate name reservation certificate
Registry fee payment receipt (approx. USD 300)
Resident agent appointment and acceptance
Identifications (passports/cédulas) of directors and subscriber
Legalization or apostille of foreign shareholder documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a negative registry qualification (calificación negativa) is issued, correct the cited observations and re-present the instrument within the statutory term, pay any re-filing fees, or appeal to the Director General of the Registro Público.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration (RUC) and municipal industrial operations license (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Alcaldía Municipal of the district where the manufacturing plant is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) application with DGI, register the company for income tax and ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios, standard rate 7%), and obtain the taxpayer certificate. Simultaneously apply to the local municipality for the Aviso de Operación / municipal business operations license covering the industrial manufacturing premises, and pay the annual municipal operating tax (tasa de funcionamiento) assessed on declared capital and business activity. Register the corporate books (Libro de Acciones and Libro de Actas) with the Registro Público as required.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed incorporation instrument
RUC application form and legal representative appointment
Proof of industrial premises address (lease contract or title deed)
Municipal Aviso de Operación application and payment receipt of municipal tax
Corporate books (share ledger and minutes book) for registry stamping
Passport/cédula copies of the legal representative and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI issues a requerimiento for missing documents, cure the file within the granted term and confirm the RUC online; if the municipality rejects the Aviso de Operación application due to zoning or surface-area discrepancies, submit a corrected declaration and site plan, and pay any adjustment to the municipal tax before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance formalities and beneficial ownership filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (Registro de Beneficiario Final); Notary Public for corporate books; licensed Panamanian bank for account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of the board of directors, adopt the first board resolution approving the registered office, officer appointments, and share issuance, and issue the physical share certificates. Authenticate the corporate books and file the annual beneficial ownership declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) with DGI identifying each natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 10% of shares or exercising control. Open a corporate operating account at a licensed Panamanian bank using the full corporate KYC package.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes adopting the attached pro-forma resolution
Share certificates corresponding to the subscribed capital
Corporate books (share ledger and minutes book) stamped by the Registro Público
Beneficial ownership declaration with passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners
Bank account opening forms, corporate KYC, and bank reference letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership filing is rejected or queried for incomplete data, submit a corrective declaration within the 10-day administrative curing period; late-filing fines may be waived or reduced upon written justification of good cause accepted by DGI.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Normas y Tecnología Industrial (DGNTI-COPANIT) for mandatory toy-safety technical regulation; Alcaldía Municipal of the plant district for the industrial operations license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Industrial Operations License (Aviso de Operación — Licencia Municipal de Funcionamiento para Industria Manufacturera), supplemented by a DGNTI-COPANIT toy-safety compliance certificate (adopting ISO 8124 series and ASTM F963) as a condition of lawful manufacture and sale of the mecha model kits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de la República de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II / Diagnóstico Ambiental under Decree No. 123 of 2009 and Law 41 of 1998; the high-precision steel injection-molding plant with plastic granulation, cooling water, and minor VOC/particulate emissions is treated as a medium-impact industrial activity requiring an environmental diagnostic and a Certificado de Viabilidad Ambiental before commencement of operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater and process cooling blowdown must comply with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 24 de 2005 effluent parameters (pH 6.0–9.0, BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L, COD ≤ 220 mg/L, TSS ≤ 100 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 20 mg/L); VOC emissions from molding presses and airborne plastic dust from granulators and finishing lines must be captured via point-source extraction and HEPA/baghouse filtration to meet MiAMBIENTE air-quality standards; non-hazardous scrap plastic, sprues, and rejected parts must be recycled or disposed under Panama's integral solid-waste regulations, with waste manifests maintained on site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection certificate issued by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá covering egress, extinguishers, sprinkler coverage, and fire-rated storage of plastic resins; structural load and electrical inspection certificate issued by the municipal Dirección de Obras and a licensed professional engineer; mandatory workplace occupational health and safety registration and clearance with MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral), including machine guarding, noise control, PPE, heat-stress management, and emergency response plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); online via the DGI Portal 'Sistema T@-Costo' and official website https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first appoint a local resident agent (agente residente) with a Panama notary public, register the notarial public deed and the 'Aviso de Operación' with the Registro Público de Panamá, then apply to the DGI for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) by submitting the corporate registration certificate, the public deed, the resident agent acceptance form, tax domicile evidence, and the DGI's Form 610 registration application; the RUC is issued within 2-3 business days and is the single statutory tax and ITBMS identification number required for invoicing and customs operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election is available for a Panama S.A.; the S.A. is an entity-level corporate taxpayer by default, but it may elect to operate under the special Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime, the City of Knowledge regime, or the Panama Pacifico Special Economic Zone regime, each of which provides bespoke tax exemptions and registration procedures, while remaining fully subject to territorial source rules for ordinary operations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) / Value Added Tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 36,000 of annual taxable gross receipts from the sale of goods or services in Panama; new businesses register when expected taxable turnover exceeds this threshold in the first year of operations, except for small contributory regimes (pequeño contribuyente) which have an optional simplified registration for gross income up to USD 36,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing through the DGI's 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SFE)' under Resolution No. 201-5429. Each invoice must be generated by an DGI-authorized billing software or online platform, submitted in XML in real time or near real-time to the DGI through authorized API channels, and include a standard 'QR' validation code; pre-printed fiscal invoices are permitted only under prior DGI 'Autorización de Impresión Fiscal' and must be reported through the 'Control de Facturación' system. No physical tax stamp is required for digital invoices, but a unique, DGI-validated folio is mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-percent ITBMS rate applies to (i) goods physically exported from Panama under a customs export declaration, and (ii) services rendered entirely outside Panama, to non-residents, or considered 'export services' under DGI rules provided that the supplier is a Panama-registered person and the service is received abroad; the seller must always maintain proof of the exportation, proof of transportation out of Panama, and, for services, a contract with the non-resident recipient and bank records evidencing foreign-source payment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / DEX)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill, or other international transport document proving that the goods left Panamanian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign bank credit advice evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in Panama within the statutory repatriation period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export zero-rating claims retroactively; failure to substantiate the physical export, the foreign banking confirmation, or the 180-day repatriation timeline triggers the reversal of the zero rate, assessment of the 7% ITBMS plus surcharge interest, and a tax deficiency penalty equal to 100% of the evaded tax; fraudulent or simulated exports additionally attract criminal tax fraud penalties under Panama's Criminal Code and suppression of the exporter's ITBMS registration for a period determined by the DGI.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no independent central bank; the banking and trust sectors are regulated by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). The territorial monetary system relies on the U.S. dollar as legal tender and the freely circulating equivalent balboa coinage.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized, open-currency regime without exchange controls. Both capital and current account transactions are freely convertible, and there are no statutory restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or repatriation of offshore-owned corporate funds. No prior SBP authorization is required for foreign exchange operations, provided transactions comply with anti-money laundering (AML) reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender requirement, no statutory conversion ratio, and no time limit for holding export receipts in foreign currency. Exporters may retain proceeds in USD or any other convertible currency and may use them freely for domestic or cross-border settlements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Merchant Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) onboarding for a Panamanian S.A. is rated 'Medium to High' with strict structural caveats. Panama's SBP does not license standalone EMIs as banks, but supervised non-bank regulated financial institutions and licensed e-money/trust operators may provide virtual IBAN services. Cross-border EMI accounts are viable for transaction settlement, but the SBP expects full AML/KYC substance verification and an appropriate registered local corporate nexus. Unlicensed foreign EMIs are not permitted to open in their own right without passported or reciprocal banking arrangements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence requirement exists in substance but is mitigated by modern SBP guidance. Trial-tier banks generally require one director or a designated corporate officer to appear for the final KYC interview in Panama, either in person at a bank branch or through a secure live video call where high-grade video identification and notarized apostilled documents are accepted. Most SBP-licensed banks retain discretion to impose a physical visit if the beneficial owner is from a non-cooperative jurisdiction or if the account is being opened solely for high-volume third-party settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-like share legacy or unregistered nominee director structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified recent register of shareholders and directors (Registro Público de Panamá), updated legalized ancestor share holding declaration, formal resolution authorizing account opening, and an unconditional compliance undertaking from the resident agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible high-volume PayPal/online retail receivables without physical trade invoice trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed revenue flow model, signed e-commerce marketplace agreements, PayPal merchant statement history, customs export declarations for plastic toy products, and a written product-institutional classification memo referencing ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership structure with zero local substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proof of Panama registered agent, physical office lease or virtual office explanation, board resolutions from the Panamanian S.A., audited annual financials, and an international tax solvency certificate from the DGI (no overdue fiscal debts).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity indicative of third-party crowd-funding or undisclosed donor aggregation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete order-level Shopify/PayPal reconciliation, count of unique customers, average transaction value, direct liability retainer policy, and audit-ready refund liability ledger clearly restricted to commercial retail sales.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from shareholders should be routed through SOLID SWIFT infrastructure: the originating bank shall execute an MT103 for USD funds destined to the Panamanian S.A. operational account, using SWIFT purpose code 'GITR' (General International Trade / Remittance) or an explanatory narrative such as 'FUNDED SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARE CAPITAL' to facilitate SBP-level AML review. Where a parent in a PAC/PAVE structure injects more than USD 10,000, documentary verification (loan agreement, share issuance resolution, capital contribution certificate) should be pre-cleared with the receiving bank. Use of USD cash or receivables-based netting is maintained within the corporate treasury ledger and should be reported to the fiscal representative as an intercompany capital movement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for commercial disbursements (e.g., payment to plastic injection mold suppliers, shipping agencies, and licensing holders) should employ SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for below-USD-200,000 invoices and commercial irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit (SILC / UCP600) for inventory bulk purchases above that threshold. Payments to China-based tooling companies shall be denominated in USD and include full purchase order metadata plus NCV certificates. The SBP requires banks to retain electronic transaction records for a minimum five-year archiving runway and to confirm the underlying trade invoice when any disbursement relates to housing/retail hardware products.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD onshore deliverable forwards against COP or other Latin American currencies, available through Banco General and Banistmo desks
Offshore nondeliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Panamanian balboa (PAB) for non-resident counterparties not requiring SBP authorization
Cross-currency swap facilities for CNY/USD exposure arising from Chinese plastic moulding tooling imports
Plain-vanilla FX swap contracts between CNY and USD, permitted without exchange-control constraints

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax of Legal Persons (Impuesto de Franquicia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 31 October of each calendar year for the preceding fiscal year (for an S.A. with a 31 December year-end, by 31 October).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 10% to 15% on unpaid tax, monthly interest of 1%, and a fine of USD 100 or more; repeated non-payment leads to DGI collection orders, impediment to obtaining Paz y Salvo tax clearance, and after continued negligence administrative strike-off of the corporation from the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Corporate Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end the return is due on or before 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines from USD 50 to USD 500 plus monthly surcharge of up to 10% of the tax due; failure to file enables a DGI anti-suppression assessment, asset attachment, and cancellation of the Open Business Standing (Paz y Salvo), leading eventually to compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), via licensed Resident Agent electronic submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The Resident Agent files an annual consolidated UBO confirmation for each S.A. no later than 31 May of each year; share transfers occurring during the year must be incorporated into that annual confirmation, with an interim update due no later than 30 days after a transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false declarations attract administrative fines (aggregate up to USD 10,000 per non-filing under current UBO regulations); repeated non-compliance may result in a memo on the Public Registry file and disqualification against the Resident Agent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered when (i) gross annual taxable income or total annual sales exceed USD 1,500,000; (ii) the S.A. is a regulated bank, insurer, securities issuer, trust licensee, or special license; (iii) DGI classifies the entity as a 'large taxpayer'. Entities below these thresholds are not required to submit audited financial statements with the DGI unless specifically notified.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (full International Financial Reporting Standards) applies to all Panamanian corporations for annual financial reporting; SMEs may apply the IFRS for SMEs standard. Accounting records must be kept in Spanish, with U.S. dollars as permitted currency of record.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Resident Agent must maintain a private UBO register at the registered office. Annually, the Resident Agent is obliged to confirm to the DGI through the electronic portal the names, IDs, nationality, and participation percentages of all ultimate beneficial owners. This confirmation is due within the calendar month following the annual shareholders meeting but no later than 31 May. Any transfer of shares exceeding 10% ownership is a reportable event; the Resident Agent must update the private register and submit an interim DGI notice within 30 days of the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registro de Directores y Oficiales)
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system: income from foreign sources is not taxable in Panama. No general statutory tax holiday applies to this ISIC 3240 injection-molding toy manufacturing activity; ordinary deductions for manufacturing costs, depreciation and operating expenses are allowed, and a mandatory 2% monthly advance corporate income tax credit applies against the annual assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 200 (Form 200) filed electronically through the Panama Dirección General de Impuestos (DGI) e-Tax system at www.dgi.gob.pa / www.mef.gob.pa
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company the filing deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross taxable revenue from Panama-source activities, including local sales of plastic model kits, mecha figure kits, and related replacement parts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose only revenue derived from economic activities performed in Panamanian territory; foreign-source manufacturing and distribution income is outside Panama's territorial tax scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: steel, plastic polymers, injection-molding consumables, die and mould depreciation, factory wages and any direct Panamanian production cost.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allowable deductions must be tied to Panama-source revenue; cross-border purchases of raw materials from related parties require arm's-length evidence and transfer pricing documentation if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: rent and utilities for the molding plant, packaging, domestic logistics, insurance, administrative salaries, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by invoices, actually incurred, and necessary for the generation of taxable Panama-source profit; allocations from foreign head office must be substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: gross Panama-source income minus definite and necessary deductions, under the applicable 5-year loss carryforward rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the entity generates only exempt foreign-source income, net taxable income is zero but a timely return must still be filed to preserve corporate standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable at 25%, after crediting monthly 2% advance payments, withholding tax credits, and any prior-year payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any withholding taxes applied to royalties, interest, or service fees paid to the non-resident owner are fully creditable, and uncredited balances may be refunded upon formal application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 1% on the tax due, an administrative fine of up to PAB 100 for each month of delay, and default interest at 10% per annum; false or fraudulent filings carry criminal penalties and a fine equal to twice the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid out of Panama-source taxable profits; dividends paid out of foreign-source or exempt income are not subject to Panama withholding under the territorial tax regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke any applicable Double Taxation Agreement, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the Panamanian withholding agent a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority, a complete Form of Residence (Form 28), and a certified copy of the relevant DTA. The withholding agent must file the documentation with the DGI and obtain a written administrative confirmation before applying a reduced treaty rate; otherwise the statutory 10% rate remains in force.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 10% on royalties for trademarks, patents, designs, and know-how licensed for use in Panama, and 10% on interest paid by a Panamanian debtor to a non-resident creditor, unless the interest is paid to a licensed international banking entity. Treaty-eligible recipients may obtain reduced rates (not lower than 0% and generally capped at 10%) after the DTA administrative confirmation protocol is satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panamanian Balboa (PAB): mandatory Local File and Master File must be prepared when the taxpayer's gross annual turnover equals or exceeds PAB 1,000,000 or when aggregate related-party transactions equal or exceed PAB 250,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Panamanian Economic Substance Requirements apply to entities holding income from relevant activities such as banking, financing, leasing, distribution, service centers, and intellectual property. Steel injection-molding manufacturing of action-figure model kits is not a covered relevant activity; however, the DGI and the Financial Entities Watchdog may re-characterize a non-resident-owned S.A. as a shell where there are no physical premises, no human resources, no manufacturing equipment, and no real economic risk in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring Panama-source revenues, fabricating export invoices to move profits into exempt offshore accounts, or deducting fictitious raw material purchases for the plastic model kit factory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, a monetary fine equal to twice the evaded tax, default interest at 10% per annum, and cancellation of the taxpayer's registration in the DGI active taxpayer registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or knowingly cause the filing of false annual returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficit, restitution of any illicitly transferred profits, and are subject to travel bans, asset freezes, and disqualification from acting as officers of another Panamanian corporation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Sociedad Anónima as a nominee shell with no Panamanian manufacturing plant, no local employees, and booking the action-figure manufacturing profit as 'foreign' while actual production is physically performed in a related overseas entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Where relevant activities are present, fines up to PAB 75,000 and dissolution of the entity; for non-relevant activities, the DGI re-characterizes the S.A. as a Panamanian tax resident, taxes the global manufacturing profit at 25%, and adds a 10% complementary dividend withholding on all amounts deemed repatriated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil attaches when directors beneficially receive corporate funds or knowingly execute contracts without actual economic substance; each director becomes jointly liable for all corporate taxes, interest, and penalties, and may face personal travel restrictions pending payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling injection-molded chassis parts and complete model kits to a related Hong Kong distribution affiliate at a declared price below cost, or purchasing moulding tools from a related BVI supplier at an inflated price to shift profits outside Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may adjust the taxable base under the arm's-length principle, assess the resulting 25% tax shortfall, charge 10% annual interest, and apply a penalty of up to 100% of the under-declared transfer pricing adjustment under the Panamanian Fiscal Code transfer pricing articles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or included the non-arm's-length pricing in board minutes are personally liable for the additional tax, interest and penalty; intentional structuring of such pricing is treated as tax evasion and can lead to criminal prosecution and civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform customer and source-of-funds verification on B2B buyers making wire or PayPal payments above the local reporting threshold, or accepting funds from shell customers for 'Mecha Model Kits' without physical delivery of goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Panama's Act 23 of 2015 on AML/CFT exposes the entity to administrative fines of up to PAB 1,000,000, criminal penalties of up to 8 years' imprisonment for responsible officers, confiscation of the funds, and mandatory removal from the public registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly ignore warning indicators or direct the receipt of suspicious funds without reporting are individually, criminally, and civilly liable; courts may issue freezing orders over personal bank accounts and passeports, and conviction results in imprisonment.
